extracted.intended_audience: faculty and instructional staff responsible for training and mentoring adjuncts, new faculty, graduate student instructors, and undergraduate teaching assistants in college/university mathematics departments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and ready-to-run materials for a semester-long professional development program that orients, trains, observes, and mentors novice and experienced undergraduate mathematics instructors. Covers pre-semester orientation, weekly training meetings, class visits/feedback, and materials for designing new meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and operation of an integrated professional development program
rubrics_metrics.description: the structure and operation of an integrated professional development program
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a fully-integrated model (Chapter 1 and Appendix B) combining multiple forums (pre-semester orientation, weekly training meetings, educational issues seminar, class visits/feedback, portfolios) so training can be tailored to individuals; emphasizes professional development as an ongoing process rather than a single course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-semester orientation session
rubrics_metrics.description: a pre-semester orientation session for instructors who are either new to teaching or new to a department; designed to last one day and divided into three blocks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to introduce departmental resources/traditions/conventions, course goals and administration, basics of student-centered instruction, and give novice instructors practice teaching (including videotaping and feedback). The short session can initiate issues to be resumed in weekly meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block A: Introduction to your mathematics course
rubrics_metrics.description: Block A is intended for all new instructors and introduces the teaching resources, traditions and conventions of your department
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses issues such as the goals of the courses in your department, assessment of student work and course administration; suitable for everyone new to the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block B: Introduction to student-centered instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Block B is designed for beginning instructors and serves as an introduction to the basic ideas and methods of student-centered instruction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has explicit goals (see chapter), preparatory steps and an outline to introduce and practice student-centered techniques that will be expanded in weekly meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block C: Practice teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Block C is primarily for instructors with little or no classroom teaching experience; provides opportunity for new instructors to practice teaching, be videotaped and to receive feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practice teaching activities, videotaping logistics, and structured feedback so novice instructors gain experience and formative input before the semester begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly training meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: a program of weekly training meetings combining training in nontraditional classroom techniques with nuts-and-bolts instruction issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers cooperative group work, active student participation, grading homework, proctoring exams, office hours, etc. Assumes participants have done preliminary training; selection of subjects allows quick competence in nontraditional techniques while addressing administrative responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure/components of a training meeting (meeting chapter organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: each meeting chapter is organized into standard sections to enable meeting leaders to run sessions with minimal preparation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters include: 1) Description and purpose of the meeting; 2) Goals for the meeting; 3) Preparations for the meeting (checklist); 4) Agenda for the meeting (to distribute); 5) Outline for running the meeting (detailed timeline and possible formats); 6) Ideas for expediting the meeting; 7) Suggested reading (annotated bibliography); 8) Meeting materials (handouts/background). Some meetings include multiple outlines to offer flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making In-class Groups Work
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting devoted to making in-class groups function effectively
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting includes description/purpose, explicit goals, preparation checklist, agenda, detailed outlines for running the meeting (several formats possible), meeting materials, and suggested readings to train instructors in structuring and supervising cooperative group activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting Students to Read the Textbook
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting focused on strategies to motivate and ensure students read assigned text material
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides goals, preparatory work, agendas, and outlines with activities and materials; includes suggested readings and concrete techniques (reading outlines, required questions, linking reading to assessments) to increase pre-class reading compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing and Evaluating Students' Work
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting about assessment practices and evaluation of student learning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers goals, preparation, agenda and running outline; addresses grading practices, designing assessments, rubric use, and offers meeting materials and readings (e.g., Classroom Assessment Techniques), aiming to improve fairness, reliability and pedagogical alignment of assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Homework Teams
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting on how to form and supervise homework teams
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes goals, preparations, agenda and running outlines; presents procedures and materials for introducing homework teams, managing team dynamics, and resolving common problems; suggested readings and reproducible materials provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching During Office Hours
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting that trains instructors to make office hours effective teaching opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies meeting goals, preparation, agenda and running outline; offers strategies for diagnosing student difficulties, structuring one-on-one or small-group help, and materials to support effective office-hour teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing and Maintaining Control in Your Classroom
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting addressing classroom management and authority issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explicit goals, preparatory checklist, agenda and a detailed outline for running the meeting; provides strategies for establishing authority, handling disruptive behavior, and maintaining an environment conducive to learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proctoring Tests and Examinations
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting on organizing and supervising tests and exams
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers goals, preparations (including logistical checklists), agenda, running outline and meeting materials; addresses proctoring roles, integrity issues, and practical steps for smooth administration of exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching with Calculators and Computers
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting about integrating calculators and computers into mathematics instruction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses appropriate pedagogical uses, learning goals, preparation and agenda, provides classroom activities and materials, and includes suggested readings on research and practice for technology-enhanced instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making Lesson Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting devoted to designing effective lesson plans
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides goals, preparation, agenda and a timed outline for constructing lesson plans; emphasizes aligning objectives, activities, and assessments, and supplies templates and examples for participants to adapt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies for Motivating Students
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting to generate and discuss strategies that increase student motivation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers goals, preparation and agenda items; includes concrete motivation techniques, activities to practice these techniques, meeting materials, and recommended readings about motivation and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing With Difficult Instructor–Student Situations
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting on navigating challenging interactions between instructors and students
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes common problem scenarios, goals for handling them, preparatory work, meeting agendas and outlines, suggested methods for conflict resolution, ideas for expediting the meeting, and meeting materials to role-play and rehearse responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-Semester Administration
rubrics_metrics.description: meeting about administrative tasks and wrap-up procedures at semester end
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers goals, preparations, agenda and running outline for end-of-semester concerns (grading, final exams, student records, course reflection) and supplies practical checklists and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapting Materials and Designing Your Own Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: framework and process for adapting existing materials and developing new training meetings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 16 provides a process for designing meetings from scratch, an example workshop (writing in mathematics), practical tips for planning meetings, and suggested readings; emphasizes method over content so programs can be tailored to local needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Process for Designing Your Own Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: a step-by-step process for developing new meetings tailored to program needs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes needs analysis, goal setting, design of activities, preparation checklists, pilot-testing and revision; example provided (writing workshop) and pragmatic advice for meeting leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom visits and feedback (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: procedures and rationale for conducting classroom visits—including observational visits, student feedback sessions, and peer visits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how to set up visits, what to do in the classroom, how to write reports, how to conduct the follow-up meeting with the instructor, lists advantages/disadvantages of each type, and provides a semester-long plan and practical wisdom about instructors’ reactions and common problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational visits
rubrics_metrics.description: classroom visits where trained observers watch and record teaching practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedures for conducting observational visits, including what observers should note, how to write objective reports, and best practices for delivering feedback to the instructor; includes templates and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student feedback visits
rubrics_metrics.description: visits that collect structured student feedback as part of professional development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods for obtaining and using student feedback in development: how to run sessions, questionnaires to use, processing student comments, and how to present aggregated findings to instructors constructively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting student feedback without a visit
rubrics_metrics.description: procedures for gathering student input remotely or without an in-person observer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques and instruments for collecting feedback (surveys, midterm evaluations, written comments), advice for interpreting results, and suggestions for integrating feedback into development conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer visits
rubrics_metrics.description: collegial classroom observations conducted by peers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on establishing peer visit protocols, expectations for pre- and post-visit conversations, confidentiality norms, and how peer visits differ from evaluative observations; emphasizes collaborative improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential problems with implementing class visits
rubrics_metrics.description: identifies common difficulties encountered when running a program of class visits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists problems (instructor defensiveness, logistical constraints, inconsistent observer practice, etc.) and suggests mitigations and strategies for managing resistance and practical obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for a semester-long program of class visits
rubrics_metrics.description: a recommended schedule and plan for distributing visits across a semester as part of professional development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains pacing, mix of visit types, frequency, reporting timeline, and how to integrate visits with weekly meetings and other development forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using portfolios
rubrics_metrics.description: using teaching portfolios as part of ongoing professional development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios collect evidence of teaching (materials, reflections, student work, feedback) to support growth, review and reflection; guidance covers what to include and how to use portfolios in development conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational Issues Seminar
rubrics_metrics.description: a seminar forum for discussing advanced philosophical and scholarly writings on learning and teaching
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for more experienced instructors to engage with research and theory as part of an integrated PD program; complements practical weekly meetings by deepening conceptual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A: Tips for Running Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: practical tips and remedies for common meeting problems and for running effective training meetings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies common criticisms of meetings and suggests solutions (assigning roles, dealing with disruptive behavior, meeting improvement methods including questionnaires), offers alternatives for continuing PD after instructors have 'graduated' from initial meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential elements for developing novice instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: core supports that enable instructors with little or no prior teaching experience to become competent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors' experience indicates three essential elements: the provision of appropriate training experiences; support and advice from experienced instructors; and clear ideas concerning the nature and objectives of the course being taught.
